resources.string: 4Zones listens for the Alt + Windows + 1–4 keyboard shortcuts and uses them to position the focused Samsung DeX window in one of four screen zones, so other apps do not also act on those shortcuts. It does not read screen content and does not record your typing.

4Zones uses an Android accessibility service for one thing: to detect the keyboard shortcuts that snap windows into zones (Alt + Win + 1–4 on a connected keyboard).

What it does
• Watches for the 4Zones shortcut keys so it can snap the current window.

What it does not do
• It does not read the content of your screen or any app.
• It only reacts to its window-tiling shortcuts (Alt + Win + 1–4). Other keys pass straight through to the app you're using — 4Zones does not record, store, or send that text. (A matched shortcut may be logged on your device for diagnostics only; it never leaves your device.)
• It does not collect, store, or share any personal or sensitive information.
• Everything happens on your device.

On the next screen, Android will ask you to turn on “4Zones keyboard shortcuts.” You can turn it off at any time in Settings → Accessibility.

4Zones could not open the Accessibility settings screen on this device.

To turn on keyboard shortcuts, open Settings → Accessibility yourself and turn on “4Zones keyboard shortcuts.”

You can also try again from 4Zones at any time.
